newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New South Wales sets up power sell-off committee.
newsitem.headline: New South Wales sets up power sell-off committee.

text.p: The New South Wales state government said on Tuesday it has appointed a committee of inquiry into the state's energy industry to advise on a mooted A$22 billion sell-off.
Premier Bob Carr said after a Labor Party caucus meeting the five-member committee would report to cabinet by August 18.
"The committee of inquiry will elicit views from all sectors of the community and will then report to the government with advice on the desirability of any sale," Carr said in a statement.

State Treasurer Michael Egan last Thursday circulated a discussion paper on the possible sell-off, which said it would raise up to A$22 billion, according to calculations by accounting firm Arthur Anderson.
Carr said the committee would test the Egan plan on all criteria -- "job security, consumer, environmental and regional protection and the future provision of core state services".
The proposal would allow the state to retire debt and rebuild infrastructure, but this had to be tested against retaining the asset and the concerns of the energy workforce, Carr said.
The committee, to be chaired by former ALP national secretary Bob Hogg, is to report to Cabinet by August 18 with the possibility of an early report and interim reports.
Egan said earlier on Tuesday he believed the case for a sell-off was compelling and hoped a decision could be reached by the end of 1997.

The discussion paper outlines the sale of seven power stations, six distributors, the state's high voltage transmission lines and the remaining 58 percent it holds in the Snowy Mountains Hydroelectric Authority.
The proposal faces opposition from the Left of the Labor Party, which is committed to public ownership, and from power industry trade unions.
